coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

changes.text: Mission Bay third real-buildings pass: geometrically scanned all 96 sizeable OSM/DataSF building footprints inside the official Mission Bay North/South redevelopment-area boundary against every already-tracked record; found 12 real, in-boundary buildings still uncovered and added them as real footprints (geometry sourced from DataSF Building Footprints, name/address cross-referenced via OpenStreetMap): MB360, Channel Mission Bay, Strata at Mission Bay, J. David Gladstone Institutes, Crescent Cove, Mission Walk (330 and 335 Berry St), Venue, 500 Terry A. Francois Boulevard, 1500 and 1700 Owens St, and the Mission Creek Park Pavilion. Two office buildings that scanned as 'uncovered' (China Basin's Wharfside/Berry Buildings at 185 Berry St, and the Bay View Boat Club at 489 Terry Francois Blvd) were investigated and excluded: both sit mostly (88-100%) outside the official redevelopment-area boundary, so they are not in scope even though they touch it. Mission Walk (330 Berry St)'s DataSF footprint originally overlapped the already-committed Arterra building by 712 sq m (caught by check_geometry_quality.py --strict); trimmed to the non-overlapping remainder rather than left overlapping or guessed. The real, notable Edwin M. Lee Apartments (1150 3rd St) was investigated but could not be confidently separated from Venue's footprint in the available data and was left out rather than guessed. Record dossiers deferred to a follow-up pass, matching the UCSF geometry-then-dossiers precedent.

Ground-level 'now' photo added for Building G (Visa headquarters) -- previously relied only on the shared Mission Rock site aerial, no photo of the building itself. Openly licensed Wikimedia Commons photograph (CC0), license read and recorded on the entry.

A second, more recent (2020) 'now' photo of Pier 48's exterior added alongside the existing 2013 Historic Resource Evaluation photo. Openly licensed Wikimedia Commons photograph (CC BY-SA 4.0), license read and recorded on the entry.

Pier 70 first-photo pass: five records that had only a 2013 site-plan document (or nothing photographic at all) gained a real, openly licensed photograph -- Building 101 (RH's Palm Court restaurant interior), Building 104, the Union Iron Works Machine Shop/Foundry (Buildings 113/114 and 115/116), Irish Hill Playground and the Waterfront Open Space. Licenses read and recorded on each entry.

Potrero Power Station had zero geotagged Wikimedia Commons candidates near any of its 22 tracked records (a fenced, long-inaccessible former power plant site, unlike Pier 70's public shipyard grounds) -- extracted three unhosted renderings straight from the project's own Draft EIR instead (Case No. 2017-011878ENV, Oct 2018, by Steelblue LLC): Waterfront Park, Power Station Park and Humboldt Street Plaza each gain a perspective rendering alongside their existing plan-diagram figure.

Building 12's status.csv source citation pointed at this private build-pipeline repository's own GitHub copy of status.csv, which is never public. Repointed to the same file's copy in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record/blob/main/data/status.csv), which is what a reader of the citation can actually open.
Chase Center gained its first two photos -- an exterior and an interior arena shot -- having had zero images of any kind before this.
The UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay hospital complex gained two exterior entrance photos, having previously had only a 2008 UC Regents site-plan document.

record.name: UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay

changes.text: Mission Bay photo pass: of 272 Wikimedia Commons candidates across 31 records, 189 were near a record with no dossier file yet (an image entry needs a record file to attach to) and 41 were geosearch false positives (Chase Center, Pier 50, Muni platforms and other nearby features that aren't the target record). The 6 that survived triage are recorded above.

Crane Cove Park gained three photos (two now, one before showing the preserved cranes in their pre-park fenced yard) -- previously only a 2015 schematic-design document. These four candidates, plus a Building 101 exterior shot, were identified during the Pier 70 photo pass but deferred there after Wikimedia's origin server rate-limited full-resolution downloads all session; recovered via the same thumbnail-path workaround used for Mission Bay once the API's query endpoint (not just the upload endpoint) had cleared.
A second now photo added: the building's entrance doors, with its 590 address plate visible, complementing the previously hosted Palm Court interior shot.
Verde's first retail-tenant photo: a Mapillary street-level frame showing Ike's Love & Sandwiches' storefront signage at the 1090 Bridgeview Way corner, tagged subject: retail:ikes-love-sandwiches.

Mission Rock photo pass, first with Mapillary enabled: of 487 candidates (46 Wikimedia Commons, 441 Mapillary), one survived triage (Verde's Ike's Love & Sandwiches storefront). All 14 dossier-backed records already had a current photo from the earlier Commons pass, so most Mapillary frames -- a systematic marker_geo road-survey pass plus an older bike-mounted fisheye series -- were street/pavement views that didn't add anything; a real ATwater Tavern storefront was found but not hosted since no source ties that business to the Pier 48 (8719A001) parcel, whose own dossier says its retail space has been unleased since Anchor Brewing closed in 2023. The other 7 shot-list rows still have no dossier file to attach an image to.

Mission Rock labeled map: replaced the thin real-street centerline highlight with the real street CORRIDOR (the same curb+centerline buffer join_approximate.py clips against), after the owner flagged Blocks D1/D2/H as appearing to eat the Mission Rock Street sidewalk on sign-off. Measured directly against DataSF's real curb and centerline data: the blocks' south edge (the recorded Assessor lot line) sits ~9.5-10.3m from the street centerline, real curb ~7.2-7.8m -- a genuine ~2.7-3.5m sidewalk gap the blocks already stop short of. No geometry changed; only the map's street rendering, which previously implied a much narrower street than the real right-of-way.

changes.text: Mission Rock labeled map, round 2: the round-1 street-corridor fix above unioned in a real DataSF curb LineString that turns out to cover only part of Block H's Mission Rock St frontage, pulling the rendered street edge in tight under part of H (~1.2m gap) while the rest of the D1/D2/H frontage kept the generic ~3.9-4.3m gap -- a false pinch/step the owner flagged as looking wrong ('should be a straight line'). Checked the block geometry first rather than assume it was wrong: D1, D2 and H's south edges are collinear to within millimeters from their own committed coordinates, and the pure centerline buffer (no curb) already runs as one continuous straight band the full frontage length at the same bearing. Added an include_curbs flag to street_geometry.build_street_buffer() (default True, unchanged for every clipping/QA caller) and set it False only for this one map's rendering, so a partial curb segment can't make an already-straight real street look broken on the one map built to show it plainly. No geometry or clipping logic changed.

changes.text: Pier 48's dossier (data/records/9900048.json) was never renamed to match the 8719A001 lot correction above, so it sat orphaned until the site build's strict record-id check caught it while regenerating the site after merging main. Renamed to data/records/8719A001.json and updated its internal record_id field to match; no other content changed.

Mission Bay is now a real site: boundary sourced from DataSF's official redevelopment-project-area layer (Mission Bay North + South), config.py's bbox extended west to cover it, and 6 real Assessor-parcel records (Block 12 West, the Public Safety Building, Block 9, Block 9A, Mission Bay School, Chase Center) plus 5 real park boundaries added. Placeholder removed.

Block 4 East's site label normalized from "Mission Bay South Block 4 East" to "Mission Bay South", matching the one-label-per-site convention every other site uses, now that Mission Bay South has more than one record.

Chase Center promoted from an orientation-only landmark to a tracked record on its real, active parcel (blklot 8722025). The landmark row it replaces had pointed at blklot 8722001, a retired/superseded Assessor parcel -- not caught until this pass cross-checked it against a fresh parcel fetch.

Mission Bay second pass: record dossiers written for the 6 milestone-one records (Block 12 West, the Public Safety Building, HomeRise/Block 9, Block 9A, Mission Bay School, Chase Center); 6 more real, active Assessor-parcel status.csv rows added for already-complete Mission Bay South office/residential/hospitality buildings (The Exchange on 16th, Uber Mission Bay 1/2, the combined Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 record, Azure Apartments, LUMA Hotel), each confirmed against the DataSF Assessor tax-roll dataset; and 8 real OpenStreetMap building footprints added for named residential towers whose underlying Assessor parcels are condo-mapped across many per-unit lots (no single blklot represents the building) -- The Beacon, the three Avalon at Mission Bay phases, Madrone, Arden, One Mission Bay and Radiance. Point-in-polygon checked against the official Mission Bay North/South boundary: several of these (Madrone, Arden, One Mission Bay, Radiance, and the 6 new status.csv records) fall in Mission Bay South, correcting this project's own brief, which had informally grouped them under 'Mission Bay North.'

Mission Bay UCSF campus pass: 14 real OpenStreetMap building footprints added for UCSF's Mission Bay campus (the hospital complex housing Benioff Children's/Bakar Cancer/Betty Irene Moore Women's Hospital, 6 research/academic buildings -- Genentech Hall, Rock Hall, Byers Hall, Sandler Neurosciences Center, Smith Cardiovascular Research Building, Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building -- Mission Hall, the William J. Rutter Community Center, the Mission Bay Preliminary Utilities Plant, and 4 student/faculty housing buildings). Investigated the campus's actual parcel structure rather than assuming the brief's 'hundreds of condo parcels' description: it's several large real Assessor land parcels each spanning multiple buildings (the opposite of Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers), so real building footprints are the correct, non-overlapping geometry, the same pattern as Pier 70's Building 14 precedent. One raw-vs-processed gap (Genentech Hall <-> Byers Hall) explained by real DataSF curb data and whitelisted in check_raw_vs_processed_touching.py with an updated, reason-agnostic accepted-pair comment.

Record dossiers written for the 14 UCSF Mission Bay campus buildings added in the prior pass (the hospital complex, 6 research/academic buildings, the community center, the utilities plant, and the 4-building student/faculty housing complex), sourced from UCSF's own press releases, architect/contractor/engineer project pages, and UCSF's historical archive. Two corrections to this thread's own earlier assumptions carried over from the geometry pass (Sandler Neurosciences Center opened 2012 not 2011; the hospital's architect is Anshen+Allen/Stantec, not Perkins&Will); unresolved discrepancies (Rock Hall's opening year, Mission Hall's street address, the Utilities Plant's construction date and address) left in each dossier's open_questions rather than picked arbitrarily.

Kaiser Permanente Mission Bay Medical Offices added as a real, active Assessor-parcel record (blklot 8709020, 1600 Owens St) -- an outpatient medical office building Kaiser purchased outright from developer/fee-manager Alexandria Real Estate Equities in Dec 2013, opened March 2016. Stories (9 vs 10), square footage (200,000-250,884 sq ft) and LEED rating (Platinum vs Gold) are contested across sources and left unresolved rather than picked arbitrarily.

record.name: Kaiser Permanente San Francisco Mission Bay Medical Offices

changes.text: Mission Bay Branch Library added as a real, active Assessor-parcel record (blklot 8708110, 960 4th St, built 2005) -- the Assessor tax roll's own property_location field for this blklot reads '201 BERRY ST', a stale corner-frontage address rather than the library's current 4th St address, the same kind of discrepancy already documented for The Exchange on 16th.

UCSF garages pass: real OSM building footprints added for two of UCSF's Mission Bay parking structures (Third Street Garage, 1670 Owens Garage). A third named garage, Owens Street Garage, was investigated and found to genuinely overlap the already-committed UCSF hospital polygon by ~2,156 sq m on check_geometry_quality.py -- left OUT rather than added with an unresolved conflict; needs a manual satellite/site-plan check before a future pass can add it. A fourth candidate, 450 South St, was confirmed to be a private Alexandria Real Estate garage serving its own office campus, not a UCSF building at all, and was not added under the UCSF pass.

Mission Bay North pass: 5 real OSM building footprints added for condo-mapped residential buildings along Berry St not previously in the dataset -- Arterra (300 Berry St, ~275 units, 2009), Park Terrace (325 Berry St, 110 units, 2007), Edgewater (355 Berry St; developer/year/unit-count not confirmed by any source found, left as an open question), 235 Berry (99 units, 2007) and 255 Berry (2004) -- the latter two are Signature Properties' two Mission Bay buildings, informally 'Signature I/II' in some secondary sources but named here by address since neither carries that name in its own marketing. Also added Mission Bay Branch Library (see above) as the pass's one real-parcel civic addition. Point-in-polygon checked against the official Mission Bay North boundary by a research pass; several other candidates it considered (500/550 Terry Francois Blvd, China Basin Landing, 185 Channel St) were found to be South, contested, or unconfirmed and were not added.

Park P-number pass: added a p_number property (sourced, confirmed vs. inferred) to Mission Bay South's five existing real park records, tying them to OCII's own D4D/Infrastructure Plan open-space numbering (Bayfront Park = P22, confirmed; Mission Bay Commons = the OCII-named P11/P12/P13/P15/P16/P17 assemblage, exact sub-parcel unconfirmed; Mission Creek Park likely P1/P3; Mission Bay Commons interim west likely P12/P13/P15; Kids' Park likely P6). Did not split or redraw any real, community-surveyed OSM boundary to match individual P-parcels: no source found gives P-parcel-level geometry, and OSM's own mapped boundaries reflect what is actually built regardless of the underlying plan numbering. Left OUT, as documented gaps rather than guesses: P5 (Dog Park), P7/P9 (unbuilt future sports fields), P26 (Mariposa Park) and several Port-managed waterfront parcels (P18/P19/P21/P23/P24) near Mission Rock -- none had a confirmed real, digitizable footprint found in this pass.

Mission Rock's eight unbuilt blocks (C, D1, D2, E, H, I, J, K) and Mission Rock Square re-traced from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2. The earlier trace was cited to the Design Controls but linked to the 2012 proposal, and its transform (3-13 m residuals) had put the Square 26% over Verde and Block D1 on the 3rd Street crosswalk. The new transform is fitted to the four real Phase 1 lots (0.7 m RMS) and every block edge that meets a recorded lot line now sits on it.
